subject.title: [Bug]: Teams app removal/re-add retains prior DM session history

question: For true Microsoft Teams app removal/uninstall events, what retention boundary should OpenClaw enforce for the affected personal DM?
rationale: This decides a privacy boundary for retained user conversation history, and automation should not choose between non-destructive staling, proactive-reference tombstoning, or hard deletion without maintainer intent.

options.title: Stale session and tombstone conversation ref
options.body: Use the existing non-destructive session-boundary pattern, remove stale proactive conversation references, and leave transcript deletion to a separate retention policy.

options.title: Only stale the active session
options.body: This is the narrowest fix but may leave stored proactive conversation references valid after uninstall.

options.title: Hard-delete retained Teams DM data
options.body: This is strongest for privacy but needs explicit data-loss policy, migration, and stronger security review.

recommendation.title: Stale session and tombstone conversation ref
recommendation.body: Use the existing non-destructive session-boundary pattern, remove stale proactive conversation references, and leave transcript deletion to a separate retention policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Teams state-store and security-sensitive history makes this the best available routing owner for the retention-boundary choice.
